nodes.summary: The clone-size generating function `h(z) = 1 + (1 / z - 1) log (1 - z)`.
nodes.title: Closed form of the clone-size generating function

nodes.summary: The Lea–Coulson clone-size law `P(size = j) = 1 / (j (j + 1))` for `j ≥ 1` (`P(size = 0) = 0`).
nodes.title: Lea–Coulson clone-size law

nodes.summary: The `k`-fold convolution power of a sequence on `ℕ`: `p^{*0} = δ₀` and `p^{*(k+1)}(n) = ∑_{i ≤ n} p(i) p^{*k}(n - i)`.
nodes.title: Convolution power of a sequence on the naturals

nodes.summary: The Lea–Coulson generating function in power form: `exp (m (1 / z - 1) log (1 - z)) = (1 - z)^{m (1 - z) / z}` for `z < 1`, `z ≠ 0`.
nodes.title: Power form of the Lea–Coulson generating function
The clone-size law sums to one

nodes.summary: For `m ≥ 0` and `0 < z < 1`, `∑ₙ pₙ zⁿ = exp (m (h(z) - 1)) = exp (m (1 / z - 1) log (1 - z))`.
nodes.title: Lea–Coulson generating function
The Luria–Delbrück probabilities sum to one

nodes.summary: A clone founded `τ` before the end has geometric size `e^{-τ} (1 - e^{-τ})^{j-1}`; mixing over the founding-time density `e^{-τ}` on `(0, ∞)` gives `1 / (j (j + 1))` for `j ≥ 1`.
nodes.title: Clone-size law from the founding-time density

nodes.summary: The Luria–Delbrück probabilities are nonnegative for `m ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of Luria–Delbrück probabilities

nodes.summary: For `n ≥ 1`, `pₙ = (m / n) ∑_{i < n} pᵢ / (n - i + 1)` (all real `m`).
nodes.title: Ma–Sandri–Sarkar recursion

nodes.summary: The probability of no mutants is `e^{-m}`.
nodes.title: `p₀`

nodes.summary: The Luria–Delbrück probability of `n` mutants with expected mutation number `m`: the compound-Poisson law `∑_k e^{-m} m^k / k! · cloneProb^{*k}(n)`. Since clones have size at least `1`, only `k ≤ n` contribute.
nodes.title: Luria–Delbrück distribution

nodes.summary: The `p₀` method (Luria–Delbrück 1943): the expected number of mutations is recovered from the proportion of cultures with no mutants, `m = -log p₀`.
nodes.title: The `p₀` method

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
